answer: Fingerprints are counted in spiral, thus the distribution is public, and pigment lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. The declaration is a willow header, so 3915 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Each copy needs 4 hours of work. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
